title: Builder Tender, Mediation and Builder Default — Bridgewell New Home Builder Warranties Dispute Resolution Clauses
content:
Under Bridgewell's New Home Builder Warranties the builder answers first for its own workmanship and builder-period systems defects. These clauses govern the tender of such claims to the builder, mediation of a builder dispute, and Bridgewell's payment when the builder defaults.

## Clauses

**A. Tender to the builder.** When the program requires that claims go to the builder first, workmanship, water penetration and builder-period systems claims are tendered to the builder, who must respond within the program's builder response period, in calendar days, of the tender and complete an accepted repair within the program's repair completion period, in calendar days. The tender records the tender date and the date the builder must respond by. The builder's response is recorded as accepted, disputed or no response; when no response came, the response is dated at the deadline.

**B. When mediation may be requested.** Mediation is requested only when mediation is available under the program and the request is made no later than the program's mediation request period, in calendar days, after the builder responds, counting from the day after the builder's response or missed deadline with the boundary day included. Mediation is open when the builder disputes the claim or does not respond.

**C. The mediation fee.** The homeowner pays the program's mediation fee, which is billed on the claim when mediation is requested. The fee is refunded when the mediator finds for the homeowner and the program provides for that refund. The mediator's outcome is recorded as the homeowner prevails, the builder prevails, or settled.

**D. Builder default.** When the builder does not perform an accepted repair or a mediated outcome in favor of the homeowner by its deadline, and the program provides the builder-default backstop, Bridgewell pays the reasonable cost of the repair up to the program's builder-default limit over the warranty's life. Usage of that limit is the total of Bridgewell's builder-default payments on the warranty, less any reversals of them.

## Clause B judged

Clause B is judged from the company's records of the builder's response on that claim — its outcome and its date — before the request is taken.

| Builder's response on the claim | Mediation open | Request period starts counting from |
|---|---|---|
| Disputed | Yes | The day after the response date |
| No response | Yes | The day after the missed deadline |

**Boundary dates (hypothetical, 30-day request period).**

| Response recorded | Response or deadline date | Day one | Last day | Request made on | In time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Disputed | 20 June | 21 June | 20 July | 20 July | Yes |
| Disputed | 20 June | 21 June | 20 July | 21 July | No |
| No response | 31 October | 1 November | 30 November | 30 November | Yes |
| No response | 31 October | 1 November | 30 November | 1 December | No |

## Clause C in short

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Mediation is requested | The program's mediation fee is billed to the homeowner on the claim |
| The mediator finds for the homeowner, and the program provides for the refund | The mediation fee is refunded to the homeowner |

## Clause D worked through (hypothetical figures)

On a warranty whose program has a builder-default limit of 10000.00 USD, Bridgewell has already paid 7200.00 USD in builder-default payments, none reversed, so 2800.00 USD of the limit remains. The builder then fails to complete an accepted repair by its deadline, and the reasonable cost of that repair is 4000.00 USD. Bridgewell pays 2800.00 USD, the part of the cost that fits within the limit.
